McLaren: McLaren’s aero package has been tweaked for the weekend: the front‑brake duct now carries a fresh winglet to smooth airflow, the front‑corner cooling scoop is lowered to tidy up the nose and keep the engine cool, and the beam‑wing has been made “heavier” – both the single‑element and the optional double‑element versions now carry more down‑force. In plain terms, the car should hug the corners better without losing too much straight‑line speed, giving the drivers a more stable, faster‑than‑usual run through the circuit’s twists and turns.
Scuderia Ferrari: Ferrari has gone back to a pull‑rod front suspension and reshaped the wishbones and brake‑duct scoop, giving the car a cleaner airflow up front and better grip out of the corners. The sidepods are now tighter and the cooling outlets have been re‑worked, so the power unit stays cooler without sacrificing speed. Finally, a fresh rear‑wing profile and a tweaked lower element promise more stable down‑force, meaning the car should feel more planted on the straights and through high‑speed turns this weekend.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull has reshaped the front wing, nose, and front‑suspension fairings and given the floor a fresh profile – including new edge‑wing camber and shifted floor fences – to tighten up front‑end grip and improve overall downforce. A modest tweak to the side‑pod/engine‑cover shape, slimmer cooling louvers and revised rear‑suspension and rear‑wing elements aim to keep the power unit cooler and more reliable while fine‑tuning rear aero balance. In short, the car should feel more stable through the corners and stay on the limit longer this weekend, giving the team a better shot at extracting extra lap time.
Mercedes F1 Team: The Mercedes car this weekend gets a cleaner, more efficient airflow thanks to a reshaped side‑pod inlet, a deeper under‑cut on the engine cover and a lower rear‑track rod up front, which should boost straight‑line speed and corner‑exit grip. The floor, beam wing and rear wing have all been re‑profiled to improve how the car handles load, giving the drivers a more stable, predictable feel through high‑speed corners. In short, the updates aim to make the car faster on the straights while keeping it steadier on the bends, giving the team a better chance to fight at the front of the grid.
Racing Bulls / RB: Racing Bulls have stretched the nose and reshaped the front wing and side‑pod inlet to clean up the airflow at the front of the car, while a deeper under‑cut, wider cooling louvers and a re‑profiled floor give extra rear‑end grip without adding drag. The rear wing tip has been swept forward, the beam‑wing and floor fences have been nudged into a tighter position, and the whole front‑suspension layout is now a brand‑new geometry, all of which should translate into more stable cornering and a stronger exit onto the straights. In short, the aero tweaks tighten the car’s balance and the suspension overhaul gives the drivers a more predictable feel – the kind of edge that can turn a good qualifying lap into a podium fight this weekend.
Alpine F1 Team: Alpine has raised and reshaped the side‑pod inlet and given the engine cover a fresh look, both aimed at getting cleaner air into the car and keeping the engine cooler on a hot track. The entire floor – from the edge fences to the diffuser – has been re‑worked, and the rear‑corner and rear‑wing endplates have been refined to boost down‑force and stability, while new rear‑suspension fairings smooth the airflow at the back. In short, the tweaks should give the car more grip and better balance, helping Alpine fight for higher positions this weekend.
Williams Racing: Williams have fitted a set of bigger, more aggressive cooling louvre panels to the car and made a number of optional “Gurney‑flap” tweaks – on the engine cover and front wing – that can be added if extra cooling is needed at a hot track. These changes should keep the power unit and rear‑end temps down while giving the aerodynamics a tiny lift boost, meaning the car will be more stable and able to run harder through the corners this weekend.
